company_name: Jiangsu Zenergy Battery Technologies Group Co., Ltd.
overview: Zenergy is a Chinese lithium-ion battery manufacturer based in Changshu, Jiangsu, ranked among the world's top 10 (and China's top 10) power battery makers by installed capacity, with 2025 revenue of RMB8.1 billion. The company designs and manufactures EV battery cells, modules and packs (BEV/PHEV/EREV/HEV), and is expanding into energy storage system (ESS) batteries, aviation/eVTOL batteries, sodium-ion batteries and marine batteries. It listed on the HKEX Main Board in April 2025 (IPO at HK$8.27/share) and in July 2026 began the tutoring process for a follow-on A-share listing on the Shenzhen ChiNext market.

business_model.summary: Zenergy sells battery cells, modules, packs and battery management systems directly to automakers (OEMs) and energy-storage integrators on a project/design-win basis; revenue is transactional (volume x price per GWh) rather than recurring, though design-wins create multi-year platform relationships once a battery is qualified for a vehicle model. A 50%-owned joint venture (STAES, with Toyota-affiliated JV OEMs) supplies HEV battery packs and contributes meaningful equity-method profit (RMB360m in FY2025, ~44% of net income).

revenue_streams.name: EV battery (BEV/PHEV/EREV/HEV passenger and commercial vehicles)
ESS products and other (energy storage, sodium-ion, aviation)

business_model.customer_type: B2B - automotive OEMs (state-owned, multinational JV, and emerging EV makers) and energy-storage integrators
business_model.geographic_mix: Predominantly mainland China domestic sales; overseas exposure via indirect exports (batteries supplied as part of customers' exported vehicles, e.g. Leapmotor, GAC Trumpchi, and KD-parts exports with Wuling) reaching ~14% of H1 2026 revenue and rising; direct sodium-ion battery sales to EU customers are a small but fast-growing niche

competitive_position.market_position: Mid-tier challenger in a market dominated by CATL and BYD, which together control well over half of China's EV battery installed capacity. Zenergy ranked 7th in China by installed capacity in new energy passenger vehicles in FY2025, improving to 5th in H1 2026; it ranked 9th in LFP and 6th (improving) in NCM battery installed capacity domestically. The company frames itself as one of the few top-10 makers with a strong automotive-components (rather than pure battery/chemicals) heritage, drawing on its founders' background at Fuyao Glass.

moat_factors.description: Qualified supplier status on specific vehicle platforms (FAW Hongqi, GAC Trumpchi, Leapmotor, SAIC-GM Wuling, SAIC-GM, GAC-Toyota, Volkswagen JVs) creates switching costs once a battery is designed into a model, but OEMs dual/multi-source batteries, limiting pricing power

First EV battery company to obtain AS9100D aerospace quality certification; airworthiness certification for fixed-wing manned aircraft batteries gives early-mover position in the nascent low-altitude economy/eVTOL and embodied-intelligence (robotics) battery niches, markets CATL/BYD have not prioritized

NCM-LFP blended chemistry (>215 Wh/kg), polyanion sodium-ion batteries in mass production and exported to the EU/US, and various fast-charging platforms (6-8C+) provide some product differentiation versus larger peers' standard LFP/NCM lines

Far smaller capacity base (35.5 GWh at end-2025, targeting 70.5 GWh in 2026) than CATL (772 GWh plus 321 GWh under construction) means Zenergy lacks the raw-material purchasing scale, fixed-cost absorption and bargaining power of the leaders

50%-owned JV is the sole or dominant battery supplier to Toyota-affiliated HEV joint ventures in China with a multi-million-vehicle safety track record, providing a steady, high-margin profit stream insulated from EV battery price competition

weaknesses: Scale disadvantage versus CATL/BYD limits cost competitiveness and bargaining power with cell-material suppliers
Heavy reliance on continued design-win wins from OEMs in an industry where battery suppliers are routinely dual/multi-sourced
History of losses (2021-2023) and relatively thin net margins (10% in FY2025, compressing to 6.8% in H1 2026) versus scale leaders
Customer base includes financially stressed emerging EV makers (e.g., past exposure to WM Motor, which entered bankruptcy), creating receivables/credit risk
ESS and aviation businesses are still small (~5% of revenue) and unproven at scale relative to the core EV battery business

growth_drivers: Capacity expansion: total capacity to roughly double from 35.5 GWh (end-2025) to 70.5 GWh in 2026, with a Phase II 15 GWh fast-charging power battery line, a new 20 GWh ESS intelligent manufacturing project, and a March 2026 intention agreement for a 50 GWh next-generation ESS/long-duration storage project

Rising share of core customers' vehicle platforms and new design-wins (several major vehicle models scheduled to launch with Zenergy batteries in 2026), lifting domestic installed-capacity ranking from 7th to 5th year-on-year

Energy storage system (ESS) business described by management as the 'second growth curve,' with H1 2026 ESS revenue up 799% YoY (albeit off a small base), driven by 314Ah/235Ah/588Ah products and grid-scale/long-duration storage demand from AI data centres (AIDC)

Sodium-ion battery commercialization (polyanion chemistry) already exporting to the EU/US for data-centre and backup-power applications, expected to scale materially in 2026 as a hedge against lithium price volatility

Low-altitude economy/eVTOL and 'embodied intelligence' (robotics) battery niches where Zenergy holds early certification and design-win advantages (AS9100D, CAAC airworthiness, MIIT technical roadmap authorship)
Overseas/export growth as core OEM customers' exported vehicle models sell well abroad (indirect export revenue ~14% of H1 2026 revenue and rising), plus direct KD-parts exports
STAES joint venture provides a stable, growing, high-margin profit stream (HEV batteries for Toyota JVs) that diversifies away from EV price competition
Pending Shenzhen ChiNext (A-share) listing, which if completed would raise further capital for capacity and R&D and could re-rate the stock via A/H arbitrage dynamics

business.description: China's EV battery sector is characterized by aggressive pricing and overcapacity; Zenergy's own FY2025 EV battery gross margin (18.9%) and blended gross margin (18.4%, falling to 12.5% in H1 2026) show margin volatility typical of a price-competitive market dominated by much larger rivals

Revenue is concentrated among a relatively small number of automaker customers; past exposure to financially distressed EV makers (e.g., WM Motor bankruptcy) raises receivables risk, and the company has taken bad-debt provisions and reversals in recent periods
Revenue growth is tied to OEM customers' new model launches and sales success; loss of a design-win or a customer's weak vehicle sales directly reduces battery offtake

business.risk: Execution risk on rapid capacity build-out
business.description: Doubling capacity to 70.5 GWh in 2026 and further large ESS projects (20 GWh, 50 GWh) require successful ramp-up, utilization and working-capital management; underutilized new capacity would pressure margins

financial.description: Gearing ratio (total liabilities/total assets) was 61.8% at FY2025 end; interest-bearing bank and other borrowings rose to RMB5.69 billion (from RMB4.01 billion a year earlier) and continued rising to RMB7.39 billion by H1 2026, funding capacity expansion

Despite positive operating cash flow in FY2025 (RMB1.44 billion), heavy capex (RMB2.6 billion in FY2025, RMB1.97 billion in H1 2026 alone) has kept free cash flow negative, requiring continued debt/equity financing
RMB4.34 billion of assets (bank deposits, PP&E, right-of-use assets) were pledged/restricted as at FY2025 end to secure borrowings and bank facilities, reducing balance-sheet flexibility

regulatory.description: Industry demand is partly driven by government policies (15th Five-Year Plan, NEV trade-in incentive programs, new-type energy storage action plans); policy changes could affect end-demand for EV and ESS batteries

New mandatory national standards for EV power battery safety (effective July 2026) and evolving low-altitude/aviation airworthiness requirements raise compliance costs, though Zenergy currently markets compliance ahead of schedule as a differentiator
The planned Shenzhen ChiNext listing is subject to CSRC/SZSE review with no guaranteed approval or timeline, per the company's own disclosure

macro.description: Revenue is highly levered to Chinese and global NEV sales growth (China NEV sales +28.2% in 2025, +7.3% H1 2026 — a deceleration), and to the broader EV battery installed-capacity cycle

macro.risk: Lithium and raw material price volatility
macro.description: Cost of sales is dominated by lithium, cathode/anode materials and other commodity inputs whose price swings directly affect gross margin; this is also cited as a driver behind the company's sodium-ion diversification strategy

Growing indirect export exposure (~14% of H1 2026 revenue) via customers' exported vehicles, plus direct sodium-ion exports to the EU/US, could be affected by tariffs, trade restrictions or EV/battery-specific trade actions targeting Chinese supply chains

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global EV battery installed capacity grew ~20% YoY in H1 2026 to 608.5 GWh; China's domestic NEV sales growth is decelerating (+7.3% YoY H1 2026 vs +28.2% in FY2025) while overseas EV and especially overseas energy-storage demand (ESS deliveries +71% YoY globally in H1 2026, with non-China regions over half of global deliveries for the first time) are the faster-growing segments; the industry remains highly concentrated with Chinese makers now ~55% of top-10 overseas EV battery installations
macro_factors.cyclicality: High - tied to global and Chinese NEV production/sales cycles, OEM capex and inventory cycles, and to energy-storage project investment cycles, all of which are policy-sensitive
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate - the company carries substantial and growing floating-rate bank borrowings (RMB7.4 billion at H1 2026) funding heavy capex, making finance costs sensitive to PRC interest-rate moves
key_input_costs: Copper and aluminum for cell/pack components

recent_developments.event: Listed on HKEX Main Board via Hong Kong IPO at HK$8.27/share, raising approximately HK$1 billion for capacity expansion, intelligent manufacturing and R&D
Launched second-generation aviation battery (dual semi-solid-state technology, >320 Wh/kg energy density, 12C discharge, 15-minute fast charging), mass delivered to aviation customers

Signed intention agreement for a new 50 GWh intelligent flexible manufacturing project for next-generation large-capacity, long-duration energy storage batteries, targeting AIDC, long-duration storage and multi-sector (EV, aircraft, robotics, marine) applications

Announced initiation of tutoring process for a proposed A-share listing on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange ChiNext market, with Guotai Haitong Securities as sponsor; completed initial registration with the Jiangsu securities regulator

Issued profit alert/notice ahead of H1 2026 results, guiding net profit up 45.5%-81.8% YoY to RMB320-400 million; actual H1 2026 results (published later) showed net profit of RMB371.6 million, up 68.6% YoY, within the guided range, though revenue growth (71.4%) outpaced net profit growth, implying margin compression (blended gross margin fell to 12.5% from 17.9% in H1 2025)

H1 2026 (interim) results confirm ranking improvement to 5th in China by installed capacity in new energy passenger vehicles (from 7th a year earlier); ESS revenue up 799% YoY and sodium-ion battery revenue up 276.6% YoY, both off small bases
CICC initiated coverage with an Outperform rating and HK$11.40 price target (based on 26.0x 2026E P/E)
CMB International reiterated a Buy rating with an HK$18.00 price target

guidance.as_of: H1 2026 Interim Report / August 2026 profit alert

items.notes: Pre-results profit alert issued August 2026; actual reported net profit of RMB371.6 million (up 68.6% YoY) landed within the guided range

items.target: 70.5 GWh by end-2026 (from 35.5 GWh at end-2025)
items.notes: Includes Phase II 15 GWh fast-charging power battery line at new Changshu plant and a 20 GWh ESS intelligent-manufacturing project; further targeting 120 GWh by 2027 per company commentary

items.target: 100Ah, 235Ah, 587Ah and 588Ah products to achieve large-scale sales in H2 2026
items.notes: Expected to drive further growth in the ESS/energy storage segment beyond the H1 2026 799% YoY growth rate
Will produce 100Ah-class lithium metal batteries and >60Ah all-solid-state batteries for process/cost verification
Management commentary (chairperson's statement) expects more substantial order growth in 2026 as overseas (EU/US) market demand continues to be released

guidance.management_commentary: Chairperson Cao Fang's statement frames 2025 as the company's entry into a stage of 'high-quality development' balancing scale and efficiency, with ESS described as the 'second growth curve' expected to see 'full acceleration' in 2026, and reiterates intent to expand into AIDC, low-altitude economy, and embodied-intelligence (robotics) battery applications while continuing to deepen EV OEM relationships.

bull_case: Fastest-improving mid-tier challenger in China's EV battery market - installed capacity ranking rose from 7th to 5th year-on-year, taking share from smaller/slower peers even as CATL/BYD dominate the top two spots

Multiple emerging growth optionality beyond core EV batteries - ESS (+799% YoY H1 2026), sodium-ion (+277% YoY), aviation/eVTOL (first-mover certifications), and robotics applications - any of which could become a meaningful second leg of growth

Turnaround profitability trajectory - net profit swung from heavy losses (2021-2023) to RMB808.6 million in FY2025 (+788% YoY) and continued growth in H1 2026, with income tax credits and operating leverage aiding the inflection

Diversified, high-quality automotive customer base including state-owned, multinational JV and emerging OEMs, with increasing share in core vehicle models and growing indirect export exposure as those customers expand overseas

Multiple sell-side analysts (CICC, CMB International) carry Buy/Outperform ratings with price targets (HK$11.40-HK$18.00) well above recent trading levels, and a prospective Shenzhen A-share listing could provide a further catalyst and capital infusion
bear_case: Structurally disadvantaged scale versus CATL (772 GWh+ capacity) and BYD - Zenergy's much smaller capacity base (35.5 GWh end-2025, targeting 70.5 GWh in 2026) limits cost competitiveness in a price-competitive, overcapacity-prone industry

Margin compression evident in the latest interim results - gross margin fell from 17.9% (H1 2025) to 12.5% (H1 2026) even as revenue grew 71%, suggesting pricing pressure is outpacing volume-driven cost absorption

Rising leverage and negative free cash flow - interest-bearing borrowings grew to RMB7.4 billion by H1 2026 to fund aggressive capacity expansion (20 GWh and 50 GWh new ESS projects announced in 2026), raising execution and refinancing risk if growth disappoints
Customer credit risk - exposure to financially distressed emerging EV makers (e.g., past WM Motor bankruptcy) highlights receivables risk inherent in supplying newer, less-capitalized automakers

New growth segments (ESS, sodium-ion, aviation) remain small in absolute terms (~5% of FY2025 revenue) and unproven at scale, so near-term results remain overwhelmingly dependent on the competitive, lower-margin core EV battery business
